title: Oysters & Champagne Board
seo_title: Oysters & Champagne Board for Two: Raw Bar at Home
description: An oysters and Champagne board for two: a dozen fresh oysters on ice, chilled shrimp, Comté, mignonette, cocktail sauce, lemon and baguette with salted butter.
hook: A raw bar for two at home: a dozen oysters on crushed ice, chilled shrimp and one good cheese.
board_size: Platter with crushed ice + small board
why: Brut Champagne and oysters are a famous pairing for a reason: the wine's acidity and bubbles act like a squeeze of lemon on the oyster's briny, mineral taste. Chilled shrimp with cocktail sauce gives you something for the oyster-shy.
One nutty cheese, Comté or Gruyère, and baguette with salted butter turn it from an appetizer into an evening. Mignonette, horseradish, hot sauce and lemon let each oyster taste a little different.

timeline.what: Buy oysters from a reputable fishmonger; keep them cold, cup side down, under a damp towel.
Make the mignonette; chill the Champagne.
Shuck the oysters (or have the fishmonger do it within the hour).
Fill the platter with crushed ice; set the oysters and shrimp.

faq.q: How many oysters for two people?
faq.a: About 6 to 12 each, depending on whether it's the main event. The board in the book plans for a dozen oysters plus shrimp.

faq.q: Do I have to shuck the oysters myself?
faq.a: Many seafood counters will shuck them for you the same day. If you shuck at home, use an oyster knife and a folded towel to protect your hand.

Raw oysters can carry Vibrio and other bacteria, so health agencies advise against them for pregnant people, young children, older adults and anyone with a weakened immune system. Keep them on ice and eat them within an hour.
